scope: P01 opt-in Windows hub callback repair; no provider or P06 acceptance

actualEvidence.independentRerun: Prepared WSL Python -m unittest hub.tests.test_windows_callbacks.CallbackSelection -v; seven tests passed.
actualEvidence.cmdProof: windows-callback-final/cmd-result.json reviewed: six exact argv values, stdin and exit7 match; archived hash verified.

findings.detail: Callback mode still inherits legacy Ubuntu and /home/nick launcher defaults when selection variables are missing. Require explicit selection before invoking WSL; preserve defaults for ordinary non-callback invocation.
findings.evidence: Read command() and validate_callback(); existing tests do not cover missing distro/bin in callback mode.
findings.resolution: validate_callback now requires explicit valid distro, absolute Linux launcher and absolute scoped home. Independently reran seven CallbackSelection methods: missing/empty/invalid selection returns before subprocess; legacy defaults remain only outside callback mode.

findings.detail: agentmux.sh creates default HOME/.agentmux/logs and run before rejecting callback hub start. Require scoped home and route/validate callbacks before harness directory creation.
findings.evidence: Independent disposable WSL HOME reproduction: bash LF-copy agentmux.sh hub start, callback=1, explicit distro/bin/URL and missing AGENTMUX_HOME. Exit1 denied lifecycle command; default .agentmux/logs and run existed. Fixture cleaned; no user state touched.
findings.resolution: agentmux.sh routes callback hub commands to cli.py before ROOT/mkdir. Independent targeted test passed for missing and explicit scoped home: forbidden start returns failure and creates neither default nor scoped state.

findings.detail: Internal spawn marker could persist in tmux server environment and leak to later native panes.
findings.evidence: Independent isolated tmux reproduction: caller removed marker but native pane inherited1.
findings.resolution: Every pane command now unsets AGENTMUX_SPAWN_WINDOWS_CALLBACK before launch. Fresh actual same-server callback-to-native test records empty callback/internal-marker/token-file environment for native pane.

observations: Hub spawn assigns distinct per-agent token paths before launching panes and removes inherited inline token. Shell exports or unsets callback keys per pane rather than relying on shared tmux server environment.
Opt-in leaves native spawn behavior intact except stripping inherited callback-worker context; ordinary explicit native configuration remains preserved.

Real proof uses two shell panes, extracted token paths and Windows Python helper invocations through explicitly constructed WSLENV. It proves token-bound callbacks, own-work completion, cross-agent denial and revoked-token rejection.
Existing setup forwarder is unchanged. Automatic Windows-provider environment propagation and authenticated model workflows are not demonstrated.
Windows Python3 is now a required dependency of agentmux.cmd. Batch proof is bounded to supplied arguments, not every calling-shell quoting case.
Actual callback helper commands were invoked separately using captured pane context, not as model-issued commands inside a provider terminal.
limits: This is not sandboxing of same-user processes or proof that a caller cannot edit its environment.
No production NATS/plugin integration or P06 acceptance is claimed.

actualEvidence.cmdObserved: Six argv values including empty/space/Unicode/Windows-path/shell characters round-tripped, stdin preserved, probe exit7 propagated.

limitationsAfterRepair: No provider/model execution or automatic Linux-to-Windows client environment propagation was tested.
Windows Python3 remains required. Batch proof covers supplied arguments, not every calling-shell quoting case.
Native-after-callback check proves environment cleanup for this private tmux server, not multi-user security or complete cross-host isolation.
Callbacks were invoked separately with captured pane token context, not issued by a model inside a provider.
Parent owns full native/final-candidate hub evidence and phase acceptance.
Implementer reports exact fixture watchdog cleanup after real probe; reviewer verified reported hub exit, not independent process cleanup history.
